baseline_models.focus_anchor: لَنُخْرِجَنَّكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِنَا أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِى مِلَّتِنَا
baseline_models.mechanism: The two arms of the ultimatum form one jurisdictional mechanism: eject bodies beyond claimed ground or reabsorb identity into a followed creed. The possessive plurals make land and milla paired gates of collective belonging.

activation_trace.role: Outward passage supplies the ultimatum's bodily operation: forced separation from the community's claimed inside.
Ground beneath the sky becomes the material inside that the speakers mark as exclusively theirs.
Return after departure supplies the inverse operation, drawing the addressees back across the communal boundary.
A followed religion or law names the ideological enclosure into which the threatened return must occur.

changed_reading.before: The opponents offer exile or conversion as two separate penalties.
changed_reading.after: They police one boundary through complementary controls: exclusion governs bodies, while compulsory return governs identity.

baseline_models.mechanism: A public, emphatic human threat is answered through hidden divine communication with another emphatic future. The agents who announce removal become the objects of destruction, and the final label identifies their boundary enforcement as withholding a right.

activation_trace.role: Audible utterance makes the rulers' coercion a public speech act rather than an unspoken intention.
Knowledge delivered in concealment supplies the protected counter-channel through which the threatened messengers receive the reversal.
Sovereignty and mastery locate the answering decree in an authority above the speakers' territorial claim.
Falling into destruction gives the counter-sentence its terminal force and reverses who is to be removed.
Withholding or confining someone from a right gathers the threatened expulsion and assimilation under the name of wrongdoing.

changed_reading.before: The divine sentence merely follows the opponents' threat as reassurance.
changed_reading.after: The hidden decree mirrors and overturns the threat's performative force: coercers who plan removal become the party marked for destruction.

baseline_models.mechanism: Return-language does more than demand future compliance: it asserts a prior relation and scripts the messengers as deviants from a habitual communal route. The utterance may therefore seize their biography as well as their conduct.

activation_trace.role: The image of attributing what was not said or was not so opens the possibility that the threat rhetorically manufactures prior affiliation.
Return after an initial departure supplies the presupposed past that the rulers impose on the messengers.
A road worn into a visible track models milla as inherited routine whose repetition is treated as compulsory.

changed_reading.before: The demand simply means that the messengers must re-enter a creed they once held.
changed_reading.after: The rulers use the grammar of return to claim the messengers' past and make communal habit look like an inescapable origin.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier occurrences make causative exit a divinely licensed movement from darkness toward light and place it beside rescue by separation from Pharaoh. The rulers in the focus reuse that verb against the messengers, turning a liberation operation into a tool for preserving their enclosure.

activation_trace.role: Outward passage is the shared focus operation, here seized by rulers as coerced expulsion.
Withholding a right identifies the rulers' direction of exit as oppressive rather than liberative.
Outward passage here carries people from darkness toward light, supplying the constructive counter-direction.
The repeated causative passage commissions a messenger to move his people outward, making exit part of the messenger's work.
Deliverance by separation supplies the exodus mechanism that distinguishes rescue from the rulers' deportation.

structural_cues: 14:1 and 14:5 repeat causative خ ر ج from darkness toward light under divine authorization.
14:6 places that movement beside rescue from Pharaoh's coercive torment.
14:13 has rulers apply the same causative root to the messengers themselves.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated causative root and rescue-by-separation; I infer a contest over who may cause legitimate exit and toward what end. The live alternative is ordinary lexical repetition, though the Pharaoh sequence makes the directional reversal salient.

changed_reading.before: The rulers merely threaten to deport dissenters.
changed_reading.after: Their deportation counterfeits the messengers' divinely licensed exodus: they wield liberation's verb to preserve enclosure, so wrongdoing lies in authority and direction, not in outward motion alone.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding objection defines the threatened change as being turned from what the fathers worshiped. Paternal formation, submissive worship, and the accusation of diversion make return to milla the restoration of a genealogically reproduced order.

activation_trace.role: Return supplies the restorative motion by which the rulers try to reverse the messengers' deviation.
A followed religion names the inherited order into which restoration is demanded.
Turning or diverting supplies the opponents' account of what the messengers are doing to inherited continuity.
Submissive worship specifies the practice whose transmission the focus ultimatum enforces.
Fatherhood and upbringing turn the creed into a reproduced social inheritance rather than a free present choice.

structural_cues: 14:10 lets the opponents define the contested practice through what their fathers worshiped.
14:12 has the messengers choose endurance of harm instead of yielding to that inherited route.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies ancestral worship and an accusation of being turned away; I infer that return in 14:13 functions politically as restoration of genealogical order. A live alternative is that عود means becoming or entering, so actual prior adherence remains uncertain.

changed_reading.after: Return is the regime's restoration of ancestral continuity, whether or not each messenger ever personally occupied that creed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah answers the possessive land claim by promising to settle the threatened messengers in the land after the speakers. Later the current occupants can be made to pass away, and finally earth itself is exchanged. Tenure, population, and even the containing ground are therefore revocable.

activation_trace.role: Material ground is the object of the speakers' possessive claim and the substrate whose permanence is tested.
Forced outward passage is the rulers' attempted control over who may remain on that ground.
Dwelling in a home supplies the direct reversal: the threatened outsiders become settled occupants.
The same ground reappears without the opponents' possessive suffix, making it available for reassignment.
Passing away supplies the removal of present occupants and widens the adjacent succession beyond one local transfer.
One thing standing in place of another extends replacement from inhabitants to the world's ground itself.
The doubled ground occurrence marks both the displaced earth and its substitute, dissolving any absolute human title.

structural_cues: 14:14 immediately matches the focus oath with an emphatic promise to settle its recipients in the land after the speakers.
14:19-20 says present people can be removed and a new creation brought without difficulty.
14:48 replaces earth with another earth before universal exposure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent resettlement followed by occupant and ground replacement; I infer a scale progression that invalidates the focus possessive. The replacement in 14:48 is eschatological rather than necessarily the timing of 14:13, but it still limits the ownership claim.

changed_reading.before: The dispute concerns which group controls a fixed parcel.
changed_reading.after: The speakers' 'our land' is doubly provisional: its occupants can be succeeded and its ground can itself be exchanged, so the contest is not between equal proprietors.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah later classifies speech by authority and fulfillment: God's promise is true, a rival promise fails, delay is not heedlessness, and the promise to the messengers is not broken. The focus oracle is therefore not merely a louder threat but a secured counterpromise whose execution need not be immediate.

activation_trace.role: Public utterance carries the rulers' emphatic threat but does not by itself guarantee fulfillment.
Divine news and inspiration mark the answering oath as transmitted from a different source of authority.
Destruction is the promised outcome whose certainty and timing the later cues clarify.
Promise as hope opened by speech supplies the explicit comparison between divine and rival assurances.
A promise failing at its due time marks the rival speech as nonperforming and sharpens the contrast with the focus oracle.
Leaving something outside awareness is explicitly negated, so nonexecution in the present cannot be read as oversight.
Deferral to a later time supplies a gap between the revealed verdict and its execution.
The later promise explicitly belongs to the messengers and secures the focus recipients within the fulfillment chain.
Message-bearers are named as beneficiaries, reconnecting the general nonfailure statement to the threatened messengers.

structural_cues: 14:22 contrasts a true divine promise with a failed rival promise and denial of coercive authority.
14:42 negates divine heedlessness while explicitly allowing delay.
14:47 says the divine promise to the messengers will not be failed.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies promise, failure, delay, and the same recipient class; I infer that the focus oath participates in this promise architecture. The live alternative is that 14:13 is a direct oracle not formally labeled وعد, though its later fulfillment is still secured.

changed_reading.before: The focus presents two rival threats of roughly the same rhetorical type.
changed_reading.after: The divine oath is a guaranteed counterpromise rather than symmetric intimidation: delay is compatible with fulfillment, while emphatic human speech has no comparable warrant.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus rulers use speech to claim ground and force return to a communal route. The tree sequence then tests words by root, ground, stability, and fruit: a bad word is wholly uprooted from earth, while a stable saying stabilizes believers. The speakers who cover seed and threaten uprooting become ironic failed cultivators of belonging.

activation_trace.role: Uttered speech supplies the coercive word whose capacity to endure is later tested by the tree mechanism.
Covering seed supplies an agricultural image that becomes ironic when these speakers threaten agents of rooted speech.
Ground is both the claimed territory and the medium against which a word's rooted stability will be measured.
An intelligible expression broad enough to be a saying supplies the verbal entity modeled as a living tree.
Root and base supply the deep support by which a good word remains independent of coercive territorial control.
Whole removal from the root reverses the focus threat: the threatening word, not necessarily the messenger, becomes the uprooted object.
Ground reappears as the surface from which the bad word is torn, contesting the speakers' claim to stable possession.
Stability of heart, reason, and tongue explains how believers can resist the demanded return despite threatened displacement.
Saying as belief or doctrine links verbal stability directly to the focus contest over milla.

structural_cues: 14:24-25 gives a good word a firm root, elevated branch, and recurring fruit.
14:26 makes the bad word a tree uprooted from earth with no stability.
14:27 makes the stable saying the means by which believers themselves are stabilized.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the focus threat and the later word-tree test; I assign the coercive utterance as a candidate bad word and the revealed message as a candidate stable word. The parable may apply more broadly to belief and unbelief, so the identification remains abductive.

changed_reading.before: The rulers' land-backed threat is an expression of stable political power.
changed_reading.after: The threat is tested as a verbal ecology: its claim to ground can prove rootless, while refusal to return can be the effect of a more deeply stabilizing word.

context_deltas.mechanism: Those who exchange blessing for concealment are said to cause their people to lodge in an abode of ruin. This recasts leaders who claim 'our land' and 'our milla' as failed custodians: compulsory communal return may preserve their regime while housing their own people in destruction.

activation_trace.role: A followed religion supplies the communal destination that the rulers present as protective belonging.
Claimed ground supplies the rulers' apparent capacity to house, exclude, and manage their people.
Good condition and blessing supply what the leaders exchange away through their communal policy.
Covering a blessing names the exchange's failure of reception and ties it to the focus speakers.
Causing arrival and lodging turns leadership into a settlement operation with a destructive destination.
Ruin and corruption name the actual dwelling produced by the leaders' attempted preservation.
Withholding a right links failed stewardship of abundant provision back to the focus verdict of wrongdoing.

structural_cues: 14:28 gives leaders an active role in settling their people and names the destination an abode of ruin.
14:32-34 attributes earth, water, fruit, and provision to God before calling the human being deeply wronging and ungrateful.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a leadership-to-settlement causal sequence; I infer that the focus speakers instantiate that pattern of communal custody. The addressed groups need not be historically identical, so this is a structural comparison rather than an identity claim.

changed_reading.before: The rulers preserve their people and homeland by enforcing conformity.
changed_reading.after: Their enforced milla can be a ruinous housing policy: those claiming to guard collective belonging may be settling their own people in destruction.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus wrongdoers command the messengers to return into their creed. Later wrongdoers ask for delay so that they can answer the divine call and follow the messengers, while their former oath of no removal is recalled. The direction of affiliation flips after its usable time has closed.

activation_trace.role: Return is initially an affiliation movement that the rulers command the messengers to perform.
The rulers' religion is the initial destination, fixing the first direction of demanded following.
The repeated wrongdoer label links the later plea to the class named by the focus counter-decree.
Answering speech supplies the response the wrongdoers now offer after previously issuing commands.
Following behind reverses hierarchy: former commanders now propose to trail the messengers.
The same message-bearing role becomes the desired guide rather than the target of forced assimilation.
Removal from place or condition exposes as false the earlier oath that their order would not pass away.

structural_cues: 14:44 puts a plea to the Lord in the mouths of those labeled wrongdoers.
They ask to answer the call and follow the messengers, reversing the focus direction of compelled affiliation.
The same ayah recalls their prior oath that they would undergo no removal.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated wrongdoer and messenger roles plus reversed following; I infer that the later plea answers the focus ultimatum typologically. Individual speaker identity is not restated, so the reversal is class-level rather than biographical.

changed_reading.before: The ultimatum settles the immediate contest by forcing the messengers to move or conform.
changed_reading.after: It becomes the prehistory of a too-late reversal: those who command return eventually seek to follow, and the permanence they asserted is what vanishes.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus revelation reaches threatened messengers through a hidden channel; the closing ayah names the discourse a message for all people, meant to warn, produce knowledge, and awaken remembrance. Secrecy is therefore a protected relay stage rather than the decree's final social scope.

activation_trace.role: Hidden delivery protects the first transmission of the counter-decree to its threatened recipients.
Message-bearers provide the relay agents through whom privately received knowledge can enter public circulation.
Conveying a message supplies the outward completion of the hidden transmission begun in the focus.
A warning that awakens caution turns the received decree into public accountability rather than private consolation.

structural_cues: 14:13 directs concealed communication to the messengers, while 14:52 directs the resulting proclamation to people generally.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a hidden reception channel and a final universal proclamation; I infer that the focus oracle participates in that relay. The closing 'this' can encompass the whole surah rather than this sentence alone, so the model concerns channel expansion, not verbatim republication.

changed_reading.before: The revelation is private reassurance for endangered messengers.
changed_reading.after: The private message seeds public warning: protected disclosure to messengers is one stage in making the verdict socially knowable.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the focus branch names destruction and extinction while 14:17 has death arrive from every place yet denies completed dying. It remains anchored in the focus destruction verb and the immediate punishment sequence, but downstream prose should present it as pressure on mode and duration, not as a replacement definition of هلك.

activation_trace.role: Falling into destruction supplies the apparently terminal focus outcome whose mode the later scene complicates.
Loss of force and life is invoked and then denied completion, opening destruction as sustained unlivability.

changed_reading.before: Destruction means a single completed erasure or death.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it can unfold as continuing loss of life-power in which death presses from every side without granting termination.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a branch-distant material analogy: the ordinary local anchor remains milla as religion, not ash. It is still valid because the focus inventory supplies the hot-ash branch and 14:18 supplies disbelievers' works as wind-scattered ash. Downstream prose must mark the image as exploratory and never translate ملة as ash.

activation_trace.role: Hot ash in which bread is turned supplies an experimental image of creed as a communal medium that processes the returned subject.
Ash left by burning gives the disbelievers' own works the same material field but without cohesion or productive form.
A violent wind that scatters things reverses the regime's attempted conforming medium into dispersal of its own product.

changed_reading.before: Milla is only the doctrinal destination of forced return.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, it becomes a hot social bed meant to turn subjects into one form, while the coercers' own works become ash that cannot hold form.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The echo crosses roots and domains: عود governs creedal return in the focus, while ردد governs a gaze that does not come back in 14:43. It remains anchored by the shared return mechanism and the later wrongdoer scene, but downstream prose should call it a somatic reversal, not a lexical equation.

activation_trace.role: Return after departure is an agency the rulers presume they can command in others.
Coming back to a prior place is denied to the wrongdoers' own gaze, reversing command into bodily incapacity.
The blink and faculty of sight localize the failed return in the rulers' most immediate perceptual movement.

changed_reading.before: Return concerns only compelled communal affiliation.
changed_reading.after: The demand echoes forward as a lost agency: those who command others to return cannot make even their own gaze return.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is an imagistic root-to-root reversal rather than a claim that the focus occurrence means literal covering. It remains valid because the focus inventory exposes covering within كفر and 14:50 explicitly supplies covering over faces by fire. Downstream prose should preserve the normative disbelief sense while qualifying the rebound image.

activation_trace.role: Covering and concealment give the focus actors an image of agents who place a veil over what confronts them.
A cover rising over and concealing something makes the covering action rebound upon the actors' own faces.
Kindled fire supplies the agent of the returned covering and turns concealment into exposure through punishment.

changed_reading.before: The disbelievers are only agents who conceal or reject.
changed_reading.after: The covering image rebounds: those marked by concealment become the ones covered at the face by fire.

strongest_changes: Coerced expulsion becomes a counterfeit of divinely licensed exodus and is immediately reversed into promised settlement.
The possessive 'our land' loses permanence because occupants can be succeeded and earth itself can be exchanged.
The rulers' emphatic saying is tested against rooted speech and a fulfilled counterpromise, so apparent coercive stability can prove rootless.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah recurrence turned one ultimatum into a network of directional reversals: exit versus rescue, return versus later following, land claim versus resettlement, and hidden revelation versus public proclamation. Branch images also preserved material echoes that conservative synthesis would lose, especially milla as an ash-bed analogy and coverers becoming covered.
remaining_uncertainties: The focus return verb may indicate becoming or entry rather than actual prior adherence, so the imposed-past model remains rhetorical.
The tree, ash, gaze, and covering alignments are branch-backed analogies rather than lexical substitutions.
The relation between promised historical destruction, deferred judgment, and nonterminal punishment remains open.
